M0.label: Correct / No Misconception
M0.description: Learner's code is functionally correct and demonstrates conceptual understanding.

M1.label: Accumulator Reinitialisation Inside Loop
M1.description: Learner resets the accumulator variable inside the loop body, causing it to restart each iteration rather than cumulate.
M1.example_bug:
for n in nums:
    s = 0
    s += n
return s

M2.label: Print vs Return Confusion
M2.description: Learner uses print() to output the result instead of return, causing the function to return None.

M3.label: Off-by-One Range Error
M3.description: Learner uses range(len(nums) - 1) instead of range(len(nums)), skipping the last element.
M3.example_bug:
for i in range(len(nums) - 1):
    s += nums[i]

M4.label: Wrong Comparison Operator
M4.description: Learner uses the wrong comparator (e.g., < instead of > for finding max), leading to inverted logic.

M5.label: Assignment vs Equality Confusion
M5.description: Learner uses = instead of == in a conditional, causing assignment instead of comparison.

M6.label: Mutation vs New Collection Confusion
M6.description: Learner mutates the original list rather than building a new result, causing aliasing bugs.

M7.label: Index Boundary Confusion
M7.description: Learner misunderstands index boundaries when iterating in reverse, leading to IndexError or skipped elements.

M8.label: Indentation Misconception
M8.description: Learner misunderstands Python's indentation-based block scoping, placing statements outside their intended block or using inconsistent indentation.
